unitSpecialRules.name: Assault
unitSpecialRules.text: This weapon suffers no penalty 'to hit' when moving and shooting. In addition, infantry models armed with an assault weapon count as having the Tough Fighters special rule (Tough Fighters: When a model with this special rule fails to damage in close quarters against enemy infantry or artillery units, it can re-roll the failed rolls to damage)

unitSpecialRules.name: Cavalry
unitSpecialRules.text: Can dismount and fight on foot as infantry, from which point none of these rules apply - need to replace mounted figures with non-mounted figures. When cavalry, moves 9" at an Advance, 18" at Run. Cannot enter buildings or board transport vehicles unless they have dismounted. Cannot gain advantages of Down, and their cover saves are always reduced by 1. Can escape as a recce vehicle (at normal speed, not double speed). Can dismount as part of Advance move - cannot remount. Can only fire pistol or carbine (treated as pistol) when mounted. While mounted, cavalry have Tough Fighters special rule (p122- When fails to damage in close quarters against enemy infantry or artillery units, it can re-roll the failed rolls to damage). Can regroup up to 2D6" after combat.

unitSpecialRules.name: Fanatics
unitSpecialRules.text: If forced to take a morale check, they ignore negative morale modifiers from pin markers, so long as the unit includes at least two men. Remember that order tests are not morale checks. Fanatic units with at least two men left are not routed and destroyed when they have a number of pin markers equal to or higher than their morale value. When a fanatics unit is defeated in close quarters fighting, the fight counts as a draw instead and another round is immediately fought. Continue fighting until the fanatics unit wins, is completely wiped out, or is defeated and left with a single model, in which case it is destroyed.

unitSpecialRules.name: Motorbikes
unitSpecialRules.text: Moves at 12" at an Advance and 24" at a Run with the same movement rules and restrictions as Wheeled vehicles, except they may make any number of turns as they move. Cannot enter builders or board transports. Do not benefit from any advantage from going/being Down. Can react by making and escape move in the same way as recce (at normal move, not double speed). Can dismount as part of any Advance move and fight as infantry, but cannot remount. Motorcycle riders cannot shoot while moving. Cannot assault and if assaulted can make an escape move as for other recce vehicles. If attacked at close quarters each man fights as infantry (including sidecar passengers if equipped). Regroup 2D6" rather than D6".

unitSpecialRules.name: Stubborn
unitSpecialRules.text: If forced to take a morale check, they ignore negative morale modifiers from pin markers. Remember that order tests are not morale checks, and are therefore modified as normal.

unitSpecialRules.name: The Victory Banner
unitSpecialRules.text: Any Infantry or Artillery unit within 12” and line of sight to The Victory Banner adds +1 to its morale value. Only one Victory Banner may be included in a force. A model equipped with the Victory Banner exchanges all of their weapons for a pistol. The Victory Banner cannot be given to a unit’s leader (e.g. NCOs, officers, etc), so the unit must consist of at least two figures.

unitSpecialRules.name: Tough Fighters
unitSpecialRules.text: When a model with this special rule fails to damage in close quarters against enemy infantry or artillery units, it can re-roll the failed rolls to damage.

unitSpecialRules.name: Green
unitSpecialRules.text: Green units are inexperienced and have a morale rating of 8. The first time the unit suffers a casualty, roll a die (after taking any morale checks caused by the attack). On a roll of a 1 the unit suffers an additional D6 pin markers and goes Down. There is no further effect. On a 2, 3, 4, or 5 the unit fights on. There is not further effect. On a 6 the unit is immediately up-rated to Regular with a morale value of 9 for the rest of the battle.

unitSpecialRules.name: Tank hunters
unitSpecialRules.text: If a tank hunter unit wins an assault and scores damage against an armoured vehicle, the effect is resolved on the Damage Result table as for a normal anti-tank penetration rather than as for superficial damage. In addition, these troops don't suffer from the Tank Fear rule when assaulting fully-enclosed armoured vehicles.

unitSpecialRules.name: SN-42 Body Armour
unitSpecialRules.text: Small arms (rifles, machine guns, etc), HE weapons, and close-quarters attacks suffer a -1 modifier to damage soldiers wearing body armour. Troops wearing body armour do not increase their pace when given a Run order: they run at a pace of 6".

unitSpecialRules.name: Tank Riders
unitSpecialRules.text: A tank rider unit can mount onto or dismount from a tank counting it as a transport for these purposes. Once mounted the unit is replaced by a few tank rider models placed on the tank itself. A single unit of tank riders can ride upon each tank. As with other transported units the tank riders cannot be targeted whilst they ride upon the tank; however, unlike with other transported troops, tank riders must immediately disembark if the tank they are riding upon is shot at. As soon as the firer is found to be within range of the tank, the tank rider unit immediately disembarks before the roll to hit. Units disembarking in this way are treated like units disembarking from a transport that has been immobilised by enemy fire. In addition, tank riders may not mount on a vehicle with the Recce rule (having a number of men clinging to the back of vehicle isn’t conducive to keeping a low profile).

unitSpecialRules.name: One-shot
unitSpecialRules.text: This is a disposable weapon that can be fired only once per game. Once fired, replace the model with another model that does not carry the disposable weapon, armed with either a pistol or rifle. (09-2026 errata) Once fired, replace the model with another model armed in the same way but that no longer carries the disposable weapon. If a unit of infantry includes models armeed with one-shot weapons, then each of these models is allowed to fire its one-shot weapon against a separate enemy unit. Declare the targets for all weapons that are firing at a different target before proceeding to roll for all of them separately.

unitSpecialRules.name: Shaped Charge
unitSpecialRules.text: Never suffer the -1 penetration modifier for firing at long range, nor the +1 Pen for point-blank range.

unitSpecialRules.name: Spotting
unitSpecialRules.text: The unit will spot hidden enemy units at 24" rather than the normal 12".

unitSpecialRules.name: Shirkers
unitSpecialRules.text: Shirkers count pin markers as double, for order tests, morale checks, routing, etc. In addition, they must always take an order test when given an order, even where they are not pinned.

unitSpecialRules.name: Cavalry carbine
unitSpecialRules.text: These short-barreled rifles count as pistols when used from horseback, and rifles when used on foot.

unitSpecialRules.name: Behind enemy lines
unitSpecialRules.text: When outflanking as described on page 172, unit ignores the -1 modifier to the order test for coming onto the table.

unitSpecialRules.name: Skilled riders
unitSpecialRules.text: Unit treats obstacles as open ground while mounted (except when assaulting defended obstacles).

unitSpecialRules.name: Unarmed
unitSpecialRules.text: Do unarmed models fight in close quarters? Yes they do. See the Errata document for an amendment removing a rule that previously stated that some unarmed models would not fight in close quarters.

unitSpecialRules.name: Skis
unitSpecialRules.text: Ski troops ignore movement penalties for snow and other winter conditions.

unitSpecialRules.name: Vengeance (Soviet)
unitSpecialRules.text: If the enemy force includes any Waffen-SS units, this unit gains the Fanatics special rule for the entire game.

unitSpecialRules.name: Infiltrator
unitSpecialRules.text: If the unit takes a cover save while it does not have an Advance or Run order dice on it, it receives an additional +1 to the roll. In addition, the unit might benefit from special deployment rules, as detailed in the scenario being played (see page 161).

unitSpecialRules.name: Scouts Lead the Way
unitSpecialRules.text: Units of Scouts are allowed to make a Run move after both sides have finished set-up, but before the first turn of the game. During this move, the unit cannot assault enemy units, and cannot be targeted by enemies in Ambush.

unitSpecialRules.name: HE (1")
unitSpecialRules.text: PEN: +1, PIN: D2 (D3 if in building) - Infantry and artillery can go down to halve the hits taken (rounded up).

unitSpecialRules.name: Indirect fire
unitSpecialRules.text: - cannot hit targets within their minimum range, measured from the centre the weapon itself. Units hit by indirect file receive no cover saves of any kind. However, if the target unit is or goes Down when shot at with indirect fire, the number of hits suffered is still halved. When fired against vehicles, hits from indirect fire weapons always strike the top armour, counting the +1 penetration modifier to damage regardless of the actual position of the firer. If an open-topped armoured vehicle is hit by indirect fire add the +1 penetration modifier to the roll to damage, and also add +1 to the die roll on the Armoured Vehicle Damage Results Tables. Cannot fire indirect fire weapons from Ambush. Indirect fire weapons can fire smoke (page 128).

unitSpecialRules.name: Team (2 men)
unitSpecialRules.text: A Team weapon shoots at full effectiveness so long as there are at least two team members to serve it. If only one man remains to serve a team weapon, then the weapon suffers a -1 'to hit' penalty. For squad-based team weapons, loader must remain within 1" or weapon suffers the -1 to-hit penalty.

unitSpecialRules.name: Medics
unitSpecialRules.text: If the medic's own unit, or any friendly infantry or artillery unit that has a model within 6" of the medic model itself, suffers damage from small arms fire, on die is rolled for each point of damage caused. On a 6, that damage is ignored and does not cause a casualty. Note that a medic cannot be used against damage inflicted by heavy weapons, nor against damage suffered in close quarters combat. Medic units can't fire any weapons (including those of a transport vehicle they are on), nor assault into close quarters. They will fight in close quarters if assaulted. Note that medic units and their dice are always ignored for the purpose of victory conditions, for both sides (they cannot capture objectives, they are worth nothing when killed, etc.).

unitSpecialRules.name: Medical vehicle
unitSpecialRules.text: All infantry and artillery units within 6" of the vehicle count as within 6" of a medic. Ambulances are destroyed if they end their turn closer to enemy units than to friendly units (p145)

unitSpecialRules.name: Massed batteries
unitSpecialRules.text: When rolling to determine the ‘Fire for effect!’ radius from the aiming point (usually D6+6”), instead roll two dice and take the highest score. For example, if you roll a 2 and a 5 the roll of 5 is used, so units within 5+6=11” of the aiming point will be hit by the barrage. See the Bolt Action rulebook, page 114.

unitSpecialRules.name: Flying Tank
unitSpecialRules.text: When a Soviet forward air observer calls in an air-strike, treat a roll of 4, 5, or 6 on the Warplane Type table as the ground-attack aircraft result. Additionally, if a ground-attack aircraft type is rolled, an enemy unit attempting to shoot it down requires 5 hits rather than the usual 3.

unitSpecialRules.name: Sniper
unitSpecialRules.text: If team includes a second man, the sniper rifles has the Team Weapon special rule. This means that, if the leader is killed, the second man can fire the sniper rifles, with the usual -1 penalty to hit (as well as the -1 penalty to Morale due to the loss of the leader). Unlike other units with the Team Weapon special rule, all members of a sniper team can fire any weapon they are carrying in any turn when the sniper is not using his scope, and in an assault they can use beneficial rules, like those from submachine guns, tough fighters, etc. When a sniper shoots using a Fire or Ambush order, the player can decide if the sniper uses the rifle's scope, in which case the following apply: The rifle range changes to 36". However, if the target is then found to be within 12", the shot misses automatically. The shot benefits from an additional +1 modifier to hit. Any hits go straight to damage, no cover saves allowed, and benefit from a +1 modifier on damage rolls against infantry and artillery units. If the sniper successfully rolls to hit and damage, the firing player can pick the squad leader in the target unit as a casualty. This includes NCOs, leaders of weapon teams and artillery units, officers, medics, observers, and so on.

unitSpecialRules.name: Regimental Support
unitSpecialRules.text: If team is taken in a Rifle Platoon, a second team may be taken in the same platoon (paying its costs as normal)

unitSpecialRules.name: Team (3 men)
unitSpecialRules.text: A Team weapon shoots at full effectiveness so long as there are at least two team members to serve it. If only one man remains to serve a team weapon, then the weapon suffers a -1 'to hit' penalty. For squad-based team weapons, loader must remain within 1" or weapon suffers the -1 to-hit penalty.

unitSpecialRules.name: Ampulomet
unitSpecialRules.text: If an Ampulomet hits an armoured vehicle and fails to penetrate its armour, roll a die. On the score of a 6 the vehicle is 'on fire' as described for a damage result of 3 on the Damage Results on Armoured Vehicles Tables.

unitSpecialRules.name: Fixed
unitSpecialRules.text: When ordered to Fire, fixed weapons can only target an enemy unit that lies at least partially within their front arc (i.e. within an angle of 45 degrees to each side of their barrel). Targets outside of this arc cannot be shot at with a Fire order. When ordered to Advance, fixed weapons do not move from their position, but can instead be rotated on the spot to face any direction, and can then fire suffering the normal -1 to hit for 'fire on the move'. When ordered to Run, fixed weapons that are carried and crewed by infantry teams move the normal 12" over open ground or 6" over rough ground, obstacles, etc. Fixed weapon units can never assault other units. If assaulted by an enemy, the gun itself is ignored and the crew models are assaulted as normal. Exceptions for artillery fixed weapons are listed in the Artillery section on page 123 (Any artillery piece defined as light or medium can be moved by the crew with a Run order, as normal for fixed weapons - except that these units can only move 6" rather than 12" with a Run order. Heavy and super-heavy anti-tank guns and heavy howitzers, as well as any lighter gun whose crew is reduced to a single man, cannot be moved by their crew with a Run order (though they may be rotated by way of an Advance order, as normal for fixed weapons). They can only be moved by means of a tow. Page 125 note: 'platform-mounted', 'rotating platform' or 'turntable' guns can rotate for free (no -1 movement penalty).

unitSpecialRules.name: HE (2")
unitSpecialRules.text: PEN: +2, PIN: D2 (D6 if in building) - Infantry and artillery can go down to halve the hits taken (rounded up).

unitSpecialRules.name: Tough Tank Hunters
unitSpecialRules.text: this unit has all the usual rules for Tank Hunters. In addition, they double their attacks in close combat against vehicles (i.e. each man makes 2 attacks).

unitSpecialRules.name: Dog Mines (AoSU)
unitSpecialRules.text: A dog mine is a one-shot weapon with a range of 18". Dog mines may only target stationary vehicles (i.e. any vehicle that is not sporting an order dice showing a Run or Advance order). Dog mines are fired as normal, except that instead of rolling to hit, roll on the following chart (note that if a Recce vehicle reacts to the dog mine attack by moving, the dog mine automatically scores a 2-4 result) and apply the result: 1: The dog, due to familiarity with Soviet vehicles, hits the closest friendly stationary vehicle within range instead of the target (no line of sight is needed in this case). Resolve the hit as described for 5-6 below. If no eligible Soviet vehicle apply the 2-4 result instead. 2-4: The dog is either gunned down or bolts from the noise of battle and deserts. The dog mine has no effect. 5-6: The dog scampers to the target and crawls underneath it. The vehicle suffers a hit with a Pen of +3 (no Pen modifiers or cover saves apply). ("or cover saves" February 2026 errata)

unitSpecialRules.name: Flak
unitSpecialRules.text: All enemy with the Flak special rule automatically fire at the attacking aircraft if the token model lies within their range and firing arc, regardless of whether they have already taken an action or not that turn. Flak fire does not require an action and takes place outside of the normal turn sequence. Firing a pintle-mounted machine gun flak weapon against an attacking aircraft does not make the vehicle count as open-topped for the turn. Any flak units in Ambush retain their Ambush status if they shoot at an aircraft. Hidden lose their hidden status. Friendly units must test to hold their fire (Inexperienced 4+, Regular 3+, Veteran 2+) - in case of Rookie pilot all flak units open fire automatically. Measure range - Line of Site ignored. Flak weapons not pinned hit on 5+, pinner hit on 6 - ignore all other modifiers. If HE hits, multiply as for inside a building. If 3 or more hits, shot down.

unitSpecialRules.name: Amphibious
unitSpecialRules.text: An amphibious vehicle can move directly forward only over otherwise impassible deep water at half speed by means of an Advance action. A vehicle cannot make any other action whilst moving over water - it cannot reverse, cannot turn, and will ignore all rules that otherwise oblige it to reverse or go Down. A vehicle that is immobilised whilst in the water is destroyed along with any occupants. Vehicles can shoot whilst afloat accept hull mounted weapons on vehicles equipped with floatation screen

unitSpecialRules.name: Open-topped
unitSpecialRules.text: Pinned by hits from small arms in the same way as soft-skins and infantry. If assaulted by infantry, open-topped armoured vehicles are destroyed automatically if the vehicle is damaged, in the same way as for soft-skins. If hit against top armour then add an additional +1 to the damage result roll. Note that all hits upon the upper surface of armoured vehicles count +1 penetration regardless of whether the target is open or not - so open-topped armoured vehicles suffer a double penalty: +1 penetration and +1 damage result

unitSpecialRules.name: Winter Vehicle
unitSpecialRules.text: The Aerosan can only travel over snow or flat ice – when doing so it is treated as a wheeled vehicle moving over open ground, and therefore cannot pass through obstacles. All passengers must be equipped with skis.

unitSpecialRules.name: Turn on the spot
unitSpecialRules.text: Can execute a full speed 'Run ‘reverse’ finishing the move facing in the direction of travel.

unitSpecialRules.name: Demolition charge
unitSpecialRules.text: A unit may place a demolition charge once per game by taking a Fire order. Place a marker (on a 25mm round base) in base contact with a single man in the firing unit. Once placed, if the placing unit is assaulted by an enemy, or destroyed in any way, the marker is removed. To trigger the charge, the unit must make a Run order in a subsequent turn and move at least 3" away (this cannot be used to assault an enemy unit). After the Run move is complete, the demolition charge immediately explodes, with the 3" template centred on the marker. If the marker is placed in contact with a building, when it explodes treat this as a direct hit by a 3" HE weapon against the building (and any unit inside) instead of using the template. If the marker is placed in contact with a vehicle, and it explodes before the vehicle moves away, treat this as a direct hit by a 3" HE weapon against the vehicle instead of using the template.

unitSpecialRules.name: Engineers
unitSpecialRules.text: When a unit of engineers assaults a building, the defenders cannot benefit from the defensive position bonus (see apge 110). In addition (page 296, 297): Engineering units attempting to cut barbed wire are automatically successful, but still require a Down order to do so. Combat engineers can clear an adjacent anti-tank ditch by receiving a Down order, but not as a reaction to enemy fire. Always benefit from re-roll when moving at an Advance even when crossing the enemy's minefields. Engineers receive +1 to clearing minefields (page 299).

unitSpecialRules.name: Flamethrower
unitSpecialRules.text: Hits from flamethowers allow no cover saves. When shooting with a flamethrower, roll a single die to hit as normal, but if you score a hit, it is turned into D6 hits (or D6+1 in the case of a vehicle-mounted flamethrower). As no saves are allowed, simply roll for damaage in the usual manner. Flamethrowers always hit the top armour of vehicles. Also, they don't suffer the -1 Pen penalty when firing at long range against armoured vehicles, nor the +1 Pen for firing at point-blank range. Causes D3+1 pins to target, 1 pin to firing unit. A unit hit by a flamethrower must check its morale regardless of casualties. After shooting roll a D6 (for each flamethrower fired). On a result of 1 or 2 the flamethrower has run out of fuel. Infantry: replace model with unarmed model, else remove the model instead (no morale check caused). Vehicles: no other effects. When rolling on Vehicle Damage Results table against a vehicle equipped with flamethrowers, add an extra +1 to the roll.

unitSpecialRules.name: HE (3")
unitSpecialRules.text: PEN: +3, PIN: D3 (2D6 if in building) - Infantry and artillery can go down to halve the hits taken. 10+ hits on building collapses it and kills all inside.

unitSpecialRules.name: Recce Infantry Platoon
unitSpecialRules.text: The platoon must include enough transport vehicles (either soft-skin or armoured) to transport all models in the infantry units in the platoon. All these transport vehicles may be given the Recce rule at +10pts per vehicle.

unitSpecialRules.name: Gun shield
unitSpecialRules.text: The crew counts as in soft cover from small arms hits that come from models within the front arc of the gun. Note that hits from heavy weapons, close quarters attacks, and any attacks that ignore cover saves also ignore the Gun Shield rule.

unitSpecialRules.name: Team (4 men)
unitSpecialRules.text: A Team weapon shoots at full effectiveness so long as there are at least two team members to serve it. If only one man remains to serve a team weapon, then the weapon suffers a -1 'to hit' penalty. For squad-based team weapons, loader must remain within 1" or weapon suffers the -1 to-hit penalty.

unitSpecialRules.name: Spotter
unitSpecialRules.text: Cannot be placed within coherency of the weapon crew. Either the weapon crew or the spotter can be given an order - but not both. Spotters can never assault or fire any weapon against enemy units. Spotter without an order die next to it counts as Down. (Errata 6 Feb 2025: Spotters have the Infiltrators special rule - page 120. Spotter/observer can only spt for a single Indirect Fire weapon per game turn. If firing unit switches to a different spotter it resets ranging-in process.) Cannot spot for inexperienced indirect fire weapon. When associated weapons unit is destroyed, spotter is removed also. Spotters are always ignored for the purpose of victory conditions. If spotter destroyed, the weapons team or artillery unit is not affected (other than no spotter). If already ranged in when spotter destroyed, can continue firing at 2+.

unitSpecialRules.name: Howitzer
unitSpecialRules.text: Can either shoot directly at a target drawing its line of fire 'over open sights' in the normal way, or it can shoot indirect fire. When using indirect fire, a howitzer has a minimum range; when firing over open sights it has no minimum range.

unitSpecialRules.name: HE (4")
unitSpecialRules.text: PEN: +4, PIN: D3 (3D6 if in building) - Infantry and artillery can go down to halve the hits taken. 10+ hits on building collapses it and kills all inside.

unitSpecialRules.name: Integrated Tractor
unitSpecialRules.text: This allows the gun to be moved by its crew as if it were a medium howitzer.

unitSpecialRules.name: Team (5 men)
unitSpecialRules.text: A Team weapon shoots at full effectiveness so long as there are at least two team members to serve it. If only one man remains to serve a team weapon, then the weapon suffers a -1 'to hit' penalty. For squad-based team weapons, loader must remain within 1" or weapon suffers the -1 to-hit penalty.

unitSpecialRules.name: Super-Heavy Mortar
unitSpecialRules.text: Treat this weapon as a heavy howitzer, except that it may only fire indirectly, and has a range of 12–72”.

unitSpecialRules.name: Heavy Rocket Launcher
unitSpecialRules.text: This heavy rocket launcher fires HE (4”) rockets rather than the usual HE (3”) rockets. However, to represent the fact that it is so slow to reload, after it has fired, it must then be given a successful Rally order before it can be ordered to Fire again.

unitSpecialRules.name: Multiple launcher
unitSpecialRules.text: Counts as a heavy mortar, but its chance of hitting never gets any better than a 6 (no ranging in). All units with 6" of the target and not entirely within the weapon's minimum range can be hit. If friendly unit within 6", you cannot fire and the shot is wasted. The unit firing also receives 1 pin marker. When towed, multiple launchers count as light howitzers. (Errata: 6 Feb 2025) "and its minimum range is increased to 36." (and previous Sept 2024 errata removed)

unitSpecialRules.name: Improved Ballistics
unitSpecialRules.text: Against targets within half of its range, adds +1 to its penetration value. (v3 page 56 AoI)

unitSpecialRules.name: Versatile
unitSpecialRules.text: Can also fire as a light howitzer 48"(30-60), HE (2"). (declare what shell is loaded if setting on Ambush)

unitSpecialRules.name: Versatile (medium)
unitSpecialRules.text: Can also fire as a medium howitzer. (declare what shell is loaded if setting on Ambush) (v3 page 50 AoI)

unitSpecialRules.name: Slow (only when towing)
unitSpecialRules.text: (p119) A vehicle designated as slow has a basic move rate of 6" when Advancing and 12" at a Run - only applies when towing.

unitSpecialRules.name: Internal volatile fuel tanks
unitSpecialRules.text: When rolling on the Armoured Vehicle Damage Results Tables against a vehicle equipped with flamethrowers, add an extra +1 to the roll to represent the increased risk from carrying around so much volatile fuel for the flamethrower.

unitSpecialRules.name: Fast (Tracked)
unitSpecialRules.text: A tracked vehicle with the Fast special rule has a basic move rate of 12" when Advancing and 24" at a Run.

unitSpecialRules.name: Reinforced front armour
unitSpecialRules.text: Against all shots hitting the front of the vehicle it counts its damage value a 1 higher than the damage value given in the entry.

unitSpecialRules.name: Slow
unitSpecialRules.text: Any vehicle with the Slow special rule has a basic move rate of 6" when Advancing and 12" at a Run.

unitSpecialRules.name: Tractor Factory T-34 (Factory Worker Crew)
unitSpecialRules.text: This unit must pass an order test to perform any action, even if it has no pin markers.

unitSpecialRules.name: Tractor Factory T-34 (Hastily Repaired)
unitSpecialRules.text: Whenever this vehicle would suffer Superficial Damage, it instead suffers Full Damage.

unitSpecialRules.name: Tractor Factory T-34 (No Optics)
unitSpecialRules.text: The main gun suffers an additional -1 to hit modifier.

unitSpecialRules.name: Unreliable
unitSpecialRules.text: If the vehicle suffers 1 or more pin markers as a result of an enemy attack, it automatically suffers 1 further pin marker in addition.

unitSpecialRules.name: Armoured all around
unitSpecialRules.text: No modifiers apply for penetration when shooting at the sides, rear, or from above. All shots count against the full armour value.

unitSpecialRules.name: Improved HE (heavy AT)
unitSpecialRules.text: Instead of HE (2") the heavy anti-tank gun has HE (3")

unitSpecialRules.name: Slow load
unitSpecialRules.text: The vehicle cannot be given an order until at least one other unit on the same side has already been given orders (whether successfully or not). If an army is left with a number of units which all have the Slow Load special rule, when the army receives its first order dice of the turn, put the dice back in the bag and draw again. The next dice drawn for that army can then be allocated to a model with slow load as if another unit had already been ordered.

unitSpecialRules.name: Versatile (light)
unitSpecialRules.text: Light howitzer can also fire as a medium anti-tank gun

unitSpecialRules.name: Big Shell
unitSpecialRules.text: Because of the sheer size and explosive power of its shell the howitzer has Pen +5

unitSpecialRules.name: Stationary Firing Platform
unitSpecialRules.text: This unit may only fire the multiple launcher when using a Fire order (including ambush fire, reaction fire, etc.) June 2025 errata: The vehicle may not fire if given an Advance order.

unitSpecialRules.name: Ancillary
unitSpecialRules.text: May not be given the Command Vehicle special rule for the purposes of creating an Armoured Platoon.

unitSpecialRules.name: Just a cart
unitSpecialRules.text: Tachanka move as wheeled vehicles. In addition, to represent the vulnerability of the horses, it has been given an unusually low Damage Value, and every time it suffers one or more pin markers as a result of an enemy attack, it automatically suffers one additional pin marker.

unitSpecialRules.name: Armoured Gun Boat
unitSpecialRules.text: The first time a damage roll resolved against the Bronekater equals or exceeds the Bronekater’s Damage Value, the result on the Damage Results on Armoured Vehicles table is always considered to be a 1, regardless of the actual result rolled.

unitSpecialRules.name: Waterborne
unitSpecialRules.text: May only move in areas of deep or shallow water, being treated as a tracked vehicle for speed and turning ability.

unitSpecialRules.name: Recce
unitSpecialRules.text: Can reverse at full Advance speed (instead of half speed). In addition, if shot at by an enemy unit (and has not yet taken an action that turn), it may react by immediately making an Escape move at full Run speed away from the enemy or into cover.

unitSpecialRules.name: Vulnerable
unitSpecialRules.text: Because of its light armour, all shorts to the side and rear of the vehicle get an additional +1 penetration modifier (i.e. in total, +2 for side hits and +3 for rear hits).

unitSpecialRules.name: (75mm) HE (2")
unitSpecialRules.text: Instead of HE (1") the medium anti-tank gun has HE (2") (75mm gun tanks).

unitSpecialRules.name: Easily catches fire
unitSpecialRules.text: If a roll on the Armoured Vehicle Damage Results Tables results in the vehicle catching fire add D3 pin markers rather than just 1 before taking a morale test.

unitSpecialRules.name: Improved HE (2")
unitSpecialRules.text: Instead of HE (1") the medium anti-tank gun has HE (2") - PEN: +2, PIN: D2 (D6 if in building) - Infantry and artillery can go down to halve the hits taken (rounded up).

unitSpecialRules.name: Command Vehicle
unitSpecialRules.text: Adds a morale bonus of +1 to itself and to any other friendly vehicle within 12" (not cumulative with morale bonus, and other command vehicles). In addition, when it activates, it can use one 'You men, snap to action!' extra dice on any one friendly vehicle within 12", except for other command vehicles. Command vehicles count as platoon commanders for the purpose of receiving orders from other officers.

armySpecialRules.name: The Great Patriotic War
armySpecialRules.text: Whenever a unit of infantry or artillery models fails a morale check and would otherwise be destroyed as a consequence, take the test again and apply this second result. This re-roll applies to all infantry and artillery units and not to vehicles.

armySpecialRules.name: For the Motherland!
armySpecialRules.text: Every Inexperienced unit that has one or more pin markers can make a test to lose one pin marker if there are any enemy within 12" immediately before an order is given to it. Roll a die: on a roll of 4, 5 or 6 the test is passed and the unit loses one pin marker; on a 1, 2 or 3 the test is failed and the unit retains the pin markers it has. Once this has been done, continue to test to see if the unit obeys its order in the usual way, even if they have lost their last pin marker.

armySpecialRules.name: Not One Step Back!
armySpecialRules.text: Soviet armies may include a single commissar for each rifle platoon. Commissars are political officers and do not confer a morale bonus to nearby troops. When a friendly infantry unit fails an order test within 6" of a commissar, remove one model from the unit and re-roll the dice. Note that there is no choice in the matter. The second result stands as normal - the commissar may only make a single re-roll for each unit affected. This rule does not apply to units other than infantry, and does not apply to infantry units already reduced to one or two models, or consisting of only one or two models to start with.

armySpecialRules.name: Massed Batteries
armySpecialRules.text: When rolling to determine the 'Fire for effect!' radius (D6+6") from the aiming point of an artillery barrage, instead of rolling one die roll two dice and take the highest score.

armySpecialRules.name: Lack of Radios
armySpecialRules.text: When you give the Command Vehicle special rule to a vehicle that does not have it in its entry for the purposes of choosing a command vehicle for an Armoured Platoon, you can give it the rule for free instead of paying the normal +10pts. If you do so, the vehicle reduces the radius of its Command Vehicle rule from 12” to 6”. This represents communication by means of flags or hand signals.
